title: Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
Kernel Representation and Similarity Measure for Incomplete Data
summary: The paper addresses similarity measurement between incomplete data samples, where traditional deletion or imputation-based approaches lose information or introduce bias. It proposes the proximity kernel, which combines equal-frequency binning, proximity (Voronoi) assignment, one-hot encoding, and a three-level cascading fallback strategy using kernel mean embedding for missing features. Experiments on 12 UCI incomplete datasets show the proposed method achieves the highest average NMI of 0.4245, best or second-best NMI on 10 of 12 datasets, and linear time complexity in the number of samples.

approach: Reimplement the proximity kernel from the paper for the target claim C1 on the UCI Hepatitis dataset. For each feature, equal-frequency binning uses evenly-spaced percentiles of observed values only, then each observed value is assigned to its nearest bin center and encoded as a one-hot vector. Missing feature encodings are filled by a three-level cascading fallback (intersection matching, union matching, global prior) using kernel mean embedding over matching samples. The resulting representation Z is clustered with sklearn KMeans using the ground-truth number of clusters, NMI is averaged over 10 random seeds, and nbins is searched over {2,3,4,6,8} by mean NMI. Finally, reproduce.py writes results/metrics.json comparing the selected NMI to the target 0.2289 within ±0.02.
steps: Setup: confirm numpy, pandas, scikit-learn are installed. No extra packages are required because pandas can read the UCI URL directly. Set all random seeds via the seed lists in config.

Implement src/data.py: read https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data with pandas.read_csv(header=None, na_values=['?', '']); X = df.iloc[:, 1:].astype(float).values; y = df.iloc[:, 0].astype(int).values - 1; assert X.shape == (155, 19), y.shape == (155,), len(np.unique(y)) == 2; return X, y, K=2.

Implement src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(X, nbins): for each feature j, obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]; if len(obs) == 0, centers = None and prior = uniform 1/nbins; else centers = np.percentile(obs, 100*np.arange(1, nbins+1)/(nbins+1), method='linear'); store centers and global prior frequencies.

Implement proximity_kernel.py assign_bins(X, centers): for each observed value, k = np.argmin(np.abs(x - centers)); tie breaks to lowest index; store integer bin assignments B (n, d) with -1 for missing entries.
Implement proximity_kernel.py encode_observed(B, nbins): build H_obs (n, d, nbins) with H_obs[i, j, B[i, j]] = 1 for observed entries, zeros for missing entries.

Implement proximity_kernel.py compute_fallback_encodings(X, B, H_obs, centers, nbins): for each missing entry (i, j), let O_i = observed features of i and B_i = B[i, O_i]. Level 1: S1 = {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l] for all l in O_i}; S1_j = {m in S1 : X[m, j] observed}; if S1_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S1_j). Level 2: if S1_j empty, S2 = union_{l in O_i} {m != i : X[m, l] observed and B[m, l] == B[i, l]}; S2_j = {m in S2 : X[m, j] observed}; if S2_j nonempty, h = mean(H_obs[m, j] for m in S2_j). Level 3: if S2_j empty, h = global prior for feature j (bin frequencies among observed values, or uniform 1/nbins if feature entirely missing). Store H[i, j] = h and record level counts.

Implement proximity_kernel.py build_representation(X, nbins): call fit_bins, assign_bins, encode_observed, compute_fallback_encodings; concatenate H[i, j] across j to get Z (n, d*nbins); return Z and diagnostics including missing entry count and level 1/2/3 counts.
Implement proximity_kernel.py proximity_kernel(Z): return K = Z @ Z.T / d where d = 19; use only for symmetry and bounds checks.

Implement src/cluster.py evaluate_nbins(Z, y, K, seeds): for each seed, run KMeans(n_clusters=K, init='k-means++', n_init=10, random_state=seed).fit(Z); labels = kmeans.labels_; nmi = normalized_mutual_info_score(y, labels); return mean, std, per-seed list.

Implement src/cluster.py search_nbins(X, y, K, nbins_grid, seeds): for each nbins in nbins_grid, call build_representation, evaluate_nbins, and record mean/std/per-seed; select best nbins as the one with highest mean NMI; return best_nbins, best_mean, all_results.

Implement reproduce.py: parse optional --smoke flag. If smoke, load data, subset first 20 rows, run build_representation with nbins=2, assert Z.shape == (20, 38), assert no NaN/inf, assert each observed-feature one-hot sums to 1 and each missing-feature fallback vector sums to 1, compute K and assert symmetry and diagonal <= 1, run one KMeans with seed 0, print NMI and diagnostics. Otherwise run search_nbins on full Hepatitis with nbins_grid and seeds.
Run smoke test: python reproduce.py --smoke. Verify output shows correct shapes, no NaNs, at least one missing entry resolved by level 1 or 2, and a valid NMI in [0, 1].

Run intermediate checks before full run: print X shape (155, 19), y shape (155,), class counts, total missing entries and per-feature missing counts; verify bin centers are strictly increasing for features with observed values; verify B indices are in [0, nbins-1]; verify H row sums per feature are 1 for all samples; print fallback level counts (level 3 should be rare, <5% of missing entries); verify K is symmetric, K_ii <= 1, K_ij in [0, 1]; run a sanity baseline KMeans on median-imputed raw features and record its NMI for reference.
Run full reproduction: python reproduce.py. This runs 5 nbins values × 10 seeds = 50 KMeans runs on 155 samples; each run is seconds or less.

Inspect results/metrics.json: check the C1 value, best_nbins, per-nbins means, and per-seed NMI spread. Compare |value - 0.2289| <= 0.02. If outside tolerance, run sensitivity variants: (a) percentile centers at 100*(k-0.5)/nbins; (b) percentile centers at 100*k/nbins; (c) kernel K-means assigning each point to the cluster maximizing average K to cluster members. Record each variant's value and choose the most faithful documented variant; otherwise keep the primary result.
Finalize results/metrics.json with the chosen C1 value, target 0.2289, tolerance 0.02, pass/fail boolean, best nbins, per-nbins and per-seed results, diagnostics, runtime, and environment metadata.

Class balance: print counts of y == 0 and y == 1 (expected approximately 32/123 for Hepatitis; exact counts are fine).
Missingness: total number of NaN entries and per-feature NaN counts; confirm common UCI missing markers '?' were converted to NaN.
Binning: for each feature with observed values, the nbins bin centers are strictly increasing; for any entirely missing feature, uniform prior is used.
Proximity assignment: all non-missing bin indices B[i, j] are in [0, nbins-1]; missing entries are -1.
One-hot encoding: for every sample and every feature, the encoding vector h_{i,j} sums to 1 (exactly 1 for observed, probabilities summing to 1 for missing).

Sanity baseline: KMeans on raw features with median imputation gives some NMI; record it to ensure the proximity kernel result is not identical to a trivial imputation baseline.
Parameter count: Z has shape (155, 19*nbins); for nbins in {2,3,4,6,8} this is 38, 57, 76, 114, 152 features.

"""Data loading utilities for the proximity-kernel reproduction.

Raw files are looked up first in the shared cache directory
(``REPRO_DATA_CACHE``) and downloaded from the UCI archive only when they
are not cached yet.

Only the UCI datasets needed for the claims are registered here.  Every
loader returns ``(X, y, meta)`` where ``X`` is a float array (n, d) with
``nan`` for missing entries, ``y`` holds integer class labels 0..K-1 and
``meta`` records shape / label information.
"""
import os
import urllib.request

import numpy as np

CACHE_DIR = os.environ.get(
    "REPRO_DATA_CACHE", os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "data", "cache")
)

# UCI uses '?' for missing values in these files.
MISSING_TOKENS = {"?", "", "nan", "NaN", "NA", "N/A", "null", "NULL", "None"}

SPECS = {
    "hepatitis": {
        "url": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/hepatitis/hepatitis.data",
        "cache_names": ["hepatitis.data", os.path.join("hepatitis", "hepatitis.data")],
        "class_pos": 0,
        "drop_positions": [],
        "numeric": True,
        "expect": (155, 19, 2),
    },
    "mammo": {
        "url": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/mammographic-masses/mammographic_masses.data",
        "cache_names": ["mammo", "mammographic_masses.data"],
        "class_pos": -1,
        "drop_positions": [],
        "numeric": True,
        "expect": (961, 5, 2),
    },
    "cancer": {
        "url": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/breast-cancer-wisconsin/breast-cancer-wisconsin.data",
        "cache_names": ["cancer", "breast-cancer-wisconsin.data"],
        "class_pos": -1,
        "drop_positions": [0],  # sample id column
        "numeric": True,
        "expect": (699, 9, 2),
    },
    "mushroom": {
        "url": "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/machine-learning-databases/mushroom/agaricus-lepiota.data",
        "cache_names": ["mushroom", "agaricus-lepiota.data"],
        "class_pos": 0,
        "drop_positions": [],
        "numeric": False,
        "expect": (8124, 22, 2),
    },
}


def _fetch(name):
    spec = SPECS[name]
    for rel in spec["cache_names"]:
        path = os.path.join(CACHE_DIR, rel)
        if os.path.isfile(path):
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
                return fh.read(), path
    os.makedirs(CACHE_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(CACHE_DIR, spec["cache_names"][0])
    urllib.request.urlretrieve(spec["url"], path)
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
        return fh.read(), path


def _read_rows(text):
    rows = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        rows.append([tok.strip() for tok in line.split(",")])
    return rows


def load_dataset(name):
    spec = SPECS[name]
    text, path = _fetch(name)
    rows = _read_rows(text)
    n_cols = len(rows[0])
    rows = [r for r in rows if len(r) == n_cols]

    def tok(r, c):
        v = r[c]
        return None if v in MISSING_TOKENS else v

    # labels
    labels = [tok(r, spec["class_pos"]) for r in rows]
    uniq = sorted({v for v in labels if v is not None})
    label_map = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(uniq)}
    y = np.array([label_map[v] for v in labels], dtype=int)

    feat_cols = [c for c in range(n_cols) if c != spec["class_pos"] % n_cols]
    feat_cols = [c for c in feat_cols if c not in spec["drop_positions"]]

    X = np.full((len(rows), len(feat_cols)), np.nan, dtype=float)
    for ci, c in enumerate(feat_cols):
        col = [tok(r, c) for r in rows]
        if spec["numeric"]:
            for ri, v in enumerate(col):
                if v is not None:
                    try:
                        X[ri, ci] = float(v)
                    except ValueError:
                        X[ri, ci] = np.nan
        else:
            # ordinal code = position in sorted list of observed categories
            cats = sorted({v for v in col if v is not None})
            cmap = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(cats)}
            for ri, v in enumerate(col):
                if v is not None:
                    X[ri, ci] = float(cmap[v])

    meta = {
        "name": name,
        "path": path,
        "n": int(X.shape[0]),
        "d": int(X.shape[1]),
        "n_classes": int(len(uniq)),
        "class_names": [str(v) for v in uniq],
        "class_counts": np.bincount(y).tolist(),
        "n_missing": int(np.isnan(X).sum()),
        "missing_fraction": float(np.isnan(X).mean()),
        "columns_dropped": list(spec["drop_positions"]),
    }
    exp = spec.get("expect")
    if exp is not None:
        meta["expected"] = {"n": exp[0], "d": exp[1], "n_classes": exp[2]}
        meta["matches_table2"] = bool(
            X.shape[0] == exp[0] and X.shape[1] == exp[1] and len(uniq) == exp[2]
        )
    return X, y, meta

"""Proximity kernel for incomplete data (paper Sections 4.1-4.3).

Pipeline for a given number of bins ``nbins``:

1. Eq. (4): for every feature, bin centres are evenly-spaced percentiles of
   the *observed* values, ``percentile(X_obs_j, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1))``.
2. Eq. (5): each observed value is assigned to its nearest centre.
3. Eq. (6)-(7): one-hot encoding per feature, concatenated over features.
4. Section 4.2: three-level cascading fallback (intersection -> union ->
   global prior) using kernel mean embedding to fill missing encodings.
5. Eq. (15): ``K = Z Z^T / d``.
"""
import numpy as np

# how the kernel-mean-embedding sums treat matching samples that miss the
# feature being estimated (the paper does not define h_{m,j} for those):
#   "restrict"  -> average only over matching samples with feature j observed
#                  (renormalised, keeps h a probability distribution)
#   "naive"     -> sum one-hot/estimated rows and divide by |S| (zeros for
#                  missing m), i.e. literal reading of Eq. (10)/(12)
#   "fixedpoint"-> Jacobi iterations of Eq. (10)/(12) using the full matching
#                  sets and current fractional estimates, started from priors
FALLBACK_MODES = ("restrict", "naive", "fixedpoint")


def percentile_grid(nbins):
    """Eq. (4): (k-1) * 100 / (nbins - 1) for k = 1..nbins."""
    if nbins == 1:
        return np.array([50.0])
    return np.linspace(0.0, 100.0, nbins)


def fit_bins(X, nbins):
    """Bin centres per feature from observed values only (Eq. 4)."""
    n, d = X.shape
    centers = np.full((d, nbins), np.nan)
    valid = np.zeros(d, dtype=bool)
    q = percentile_grid(nbins)
    for j in range(d):
        obs = X[~np.isnan(X[:, j]), j]
        if obs.size == 0:
            continue
        centers[j] = np.percentile(obs, q, method="linear")
        valid[j] = True
    return centers, valid


def assign_bins(X, centers, valid):
    """Nearest-centre (Voronoi) assignment, Eq. (5).  -1 marks missing."""
    n, d = X.shape
    nbins = centers.shape[1]
    B = np.full((n, d), -1, dtype=int)
    for j in range(d):
        if not valid[j]:
            continue
        obs_mask = ~np.isnan(X[:, j])
        if not obs_mask.any():
            continue
        vals = X[obs_mask, j][:, None]
        B[obs_mask, j] = np.argmin(np.abs(vals - centers[j][None, :]), axis=1)
    return B


def one_hot_observed(B, nbins):
    """Eq. (6)-(7): binary encoding for observed entries, zeros elsewhere."""
    n, d = B.shape
    H = np.zeros((n, d, nbins), dtype=float)
    for j in range(d):
        rows = B[:, j] >= 0
        H[np.where(rows)[0], j, B[rows, j]] = 1.0
    return H


def global_prior(B, nbins):
    """Eq. (13)-(14): bin frequencies among samples with the feature observed."""
    d = B.shape[1]
    prior = np.full((d, nbins), 1.0 / nbins)
    for j in range(d):
        rows = B[:, j] >= 0
        cnt = rows.sum()
        if cnt == 0:
            continue
        counts = np.bincount(B[rows, j], minlength=nbins).astype(float)
        prior[j] = counts / cnt
    return prior


def _match_sets(B, i, O, bi):
    """S1(i) = intersection of same-bin sets, S2(i) = their union (Eq. 8-11)."""
    same = B[:, O] == bi[None, :]           # (n, |O|) with False for missing
    m_all = same.all(axis=1)
    m_any = same.any(axis=1)
    m_all[i] = False
    m_any[i] = False
    return np.where(m_all)[0], np.where(m_any)[0]


def cascade_fill(X, B, H, prior, nbins, mode="restrict", max_iter=100, tol=1e-12):
    """Fill missing encodings with the three-level cascading fallback."""
    n, d = B.shape
    level_counts = {"level1": 0, "level2": 0, "level3": 0}
    level3_from_empty_level1 = 0

    if mode == "fixedpoint":
        # initialise missing entries with the global prior, then iterate
        miss_mask = B < 0
        for j in range(d):
            rows = miss_mask[:, j]
            if rows.any():
                H[rows, j] = prior[j]
        for _ in range(max_iter):
            delta = 0.0
            newH = H.copy()
            for i in range(n):
                miss = np.where(B[i] < 0)[0]
                if miss.size == 0:
                    continue
                O = np.where(B[i] >= 0)[0]
                if O.size == 0:
                    continue
                S1, S2 = _match_sets(B, i, O, B[i, O])
                S = S1 if S1.size > 0 else S2
                if S.size == 0:
                    continue
                for j in miss:
                    newH[i, j] = H[S, j].mean(axis=0)
            delta = np.abs(newH - H).max()
            H = newH
            if delta < tol:
                break
        # count diagnostics with the paper's level definition
        for i in range(n):
            miss = np.where(B[i] < 0)[0]
            if miss.size == 0:
                continue
            O = np.where(B[i] >= 0)[0]
            if O.size == 0:
                level_counts["level3"] += miss.size
                continue
            S1, S2 = _match_sets(B, i, O, B[i, O])
            lvl = 1 if S1.size > 0 else (2 if S2.size > 0 else 3)
            level_counts[f"level{lvl}"] += miss.size
        return H, level_counts, level3_from_empty_level1

    for i in range(n):
        miss = np.where(B[i] < 0)[0]
        if miss.size == 0:

        O = np.where(B[i] >= 0)[0]
        if O.size == 0:  # nothing observed: global prior for all missing
            for j in miss:

target.statement: Proximity kernel ('Ours') achieves NMI 0.2289 on the Hepatitis dataset under K-means clustering with the ground-truth number of clusters.
target.dataset: Hepatitis (UCI; 155 samples, 19 features, 2 classes per Table 2)

tolerance.why: Rule 3: NMI is a bounded [0,1] score on the Hepatitis dataset (155 examples, smaller than 2,000) and the paper prints values as fractions, so the band is 0.02 absolute.

audit_summary: The target claim C1 is reproduced end-to-end from the raw UCI Hepatitis file (verified 155×19, 2 classes with counts 32/123, 167 missing entries) using the paper's pipeline: observed-only evenly-spaced percentile bin centres, nearest-centre (Voronoi) assignment, per-feature one-hot encoding, the three-level intersection→union→global-prior cascade with kernel mean embedding, K = Z Zᵀ/d, and K-means with K = ground-truth classes averaged over 10 runs. The clean re-run computes 0.22890914 vs the paper's 0.2289 (abs diff ~9e-6), far inside the 0.02 band, and no number in the reported path is hard-coded — the paper's Table 3 row is only read at runtime from the claim contract to print a difference, never to populate 'value'. The one fidelity deviation is assumption A8: Eq.(10)/Eq.(12) are ill-defined for matching samples that are themselves missing the feature, and the implementation renormalises over matching samples that observe it ('restrict' mode), falling through to level 2 rather than using a partial sum; this is disclosed in the ledger and in metrics.json config. Categorical columns are ordinal-coded and binned like numeric ones (A1, disclosed), a plausible cause of the larger deviations on Heart, Credit and Soybean, which are extra claims, not the target. The target run itself uses the full dataset, the full nbins grid and all 10 seeds, so nothing is scaled down; however, 3 of the 12 datasets (Kidney, Horse, Adult) were not attempted, so C2/C3/C8 (AVG = 0.4245, 10/12 best-or-second) are only partially supported (9 datasets, mean 0.4458 vs 0.4583 paper on the same 9). Because the Hepatitis result is nearly deterministic (std 0 across seeds at nbins=2), the 10-run averaging is effectively a single partition there.

requirement_check.evidence: src/proximity_kernel.py fit_bins(): for each feature j, obs = X[~isnan(X[:,j]), j]; centers[j] = np.percentile(obs, q) — bin centres are computed from observed values only, missing entries excluded.

percentile_grid(nbins) = np.linspace(0,100,nbins) → percentile(X_obs, (k-1)*100/(nbins-1)) with numpy linear interpolation (assumption A2, disclosed). Structural check shows percentile_grid [0,50,100] for nbins=3.
assign_bins(): B[obs_mask, j] = np.argmin(np.abs(vals - centers[j][None,:]), axis=1); argmin default gives lowest index tie-break (A3). Observed indices verified in range.
one_hot_observed() sets H[i,j,bin]=1 for observed entries; Z = H.reshape(n, d*nbins). Structural check: Z shape (155,57) for nbins=3, per-feature sums all 1.0, no NaN/inf.

cascade_fill(): per missing entry it computes S1 (intersection over all observed bins) and S2 (union); level1 if |S1|>0, else level2 if |S2|>0, else global prior. Diagnostics record level counts (HbV nbins=3: 55/112/0; voting shows real level-3 usage: 16).

Level-1 estimate is the mean one-hot vector over S1, but in 'restrict' mode it averages only over matching samples where feature j is observed (renormalised) rather than over all m in S1 as Eq.(10) literally reads; this is assumption A8 (high risk) and is documented in the config (fallback_mode='restrict'). If no S1 candidate observes j, the code relaxes to level 2 instead of Eq.(10).

cascade_fill(): when S1 is empty (or yields no observed candidate for feature j) and S2 non-empty, H[i,j] = mean of H[cand, j] over cand in S2 with B>=0; level2 counts logged (e.g. Hepatitis nbins=2: level2=106).
global_prior() computes bin frequencies among samples with the feature observed (uniform 1/nbins if all missing, A7); applied when the union set is empty (and when no matching sample observes j).
proximity_kernel(Z,d) = (Z @ Z.T)/d, called with d = X.shape[1] (feature count, not node dimensions). Kernel check: symmetric, min 0.1956, diagonal max 1.0, within [0,1].

src/cluster.py kmeans_nmi_scores(): sklearn KMeans(n_clusters=meta['n_classes']) with ground-truth K, scored with sklearn normalized_mutual_info_score (arithmetic variant, A5). Hepatitis K=2, full-data transductive clustering (A10).

SEEDS = list(range(10)) and each nbins value is averaged over 10 K-means runs (n_init=10, k-means++). Note: on Hepatitis nbins=2 all 10 seeds give the identical partition (std=0), so repeats are effectively deterministic there; per_nbins_full records per-seed values.

NBINS_GRID = [2,3,4,6,8]; evaluate_grid loops over it and select_best picks the max mean NMI per dataset (A9, disclosed). Hepatitis per-nbins means {2:0.2289, 3:0.1718, 4:0.2097, 6:0.2104, 8:0.1967}; selected 2.

The implementation is structurally consistent with O(nd + d n log n) (per-feature percentile sort + nearest-centre assignment), but no timing-vs-n scaling experiment was run, so the complexity claim is not empirically verified.
Completed rows are strictly one-hot: structural check reports per_feature_sums min/max = 1.0/1.0 and all_one=true, so a fully observed sample has exactly d ones out of d×nbins.
